cards.question_md: Who published the first three PDAC expression subtypes (classical, quasi-mesenchymal, exocrine-like), and where?
What is PDAssigner, and why is it hard to use in a clinical trial?
cards.answer_md: The 62-gene signature of Collisson 2011 for its three subtypes. It exists only as a gene list (no centroids, no code, no rule for one new sample; re-implemented in pdacR), and the discovery cohort was partly microdissected, so a trial would need enriched epithelium and cohort-wide clustering.

cards.question_md: Why is Collisson's exocrine-like subtype considered an artefact today?
cards.answer_md: Its defining genes are digestive enzymes of acinar cells, the most abundant transcripts of normal pancreas. A little co-sampled normal tissue pushes a sample into the class, so it describes the tissue piece, not the tumour; Moffitt 2015 showed all 17 exocrine-like genes overlap his normal-pancreas factor.

cards.question_md: In Collisson 2011, which drug were classical PDAC cell lines on average more sensitive to than quasi-mesenchymal lines?
Which paper introduced "virtual microdissection" and the classical / basal-like tumour subtypes?

options.text_md: Moffitt et al. 2015 (Nature Genetics, Yeh lab, UNC)

cards.question_md: How did Moffitt 2015 separate tumour from stroma signal without physical microdissection, and what made the components interpretable?
cards.answer_md: Non-negative matrix factorisation (blind source separation) of bulk microarray profiles. The cohort mixed primary tumours, metastases, normal pancreas, distant normal tissues and cell lines: cell lines contain only tumour cells, normal pancreas none, so each factor could be assigned to tumour, stroma or normal tissue.

cards.question_md: Which two independent axes did Moffitt 2015 define, and what survival differences did they show?
cards.answer_md: Tumour axis: basal-like vs classical (median OS 11 vs 19 months, discovery; HR 2.11 in ICGC). Stroma axis: activated vs normal stroma (15 vs 24 months). Both axes vary independently, so a tumour has two labels.

cards.question_md: Which GEO series holds the Moffitt 2015 microarray cohort (357 arrays) that also trained PurIST?
Where does the name "basal-like" for the aggressive PDAC subtype come from?

options.text_md: The tumours resemble basal-like breast and bladder cancers
They sit at the basal membrane of the duct
They arise from basal cells of the acinus
They have basal (low) expression of all genes

cards.question_md: Which group published the four-class PDAC scheme squamous / pancreatic progenitor / immunogenic / ADEX?

options.text_md: Bailey et al. 2016 (Nature), Australian Pancreatic Cancer Genome Initiative / ICGC (Biankin, Grimmond)

cards.question_md: What does the Bailey subtype name ADEX stand for?
Which two of Bailey's four classes are tumour-cell programmes, and what are the other two?
cards.answer_md: Squamous (≈ basal-like, worst survival, 13.3 months median) and pancreatic progenitor (≈ classical) are tumour programmes. ADEX reflects admixed acinar / endocrine normal tissue and immunogenic reflects immune infiltrate; both concentrate in low-purity samples.

cards.question_md: What did TCGA 2017 find when it applied the Collisson, Moffitt and Bailey schemes to its curated cohort?
cards.answer_md: Analyses were heavily confounded by tumour purity. All schemes recover one contrast (basal-like / squamous / quasi-mesenchymal vs classical / progenitor); the extra classes (exocrine-like, ADEX, immunogenic) sit in low-purity samples. After controlling for purity only the classical / basal-like axis remains.

cards.question_md: Describe the two-stage design TCGA 2017 used against the purity problem.
cards.answer_md: Purity was estimated with ABSOLUTE; the 150 curated tumours were split at the median purity (ABSOLUTE ≥ 33 %): unsupervised class discovery in the 76 high-purity tumours, then supervised classification of the 74 low-purity tumours with classifiers trained on the pure ones.

cards.question_md: How many tumours of TCGA-PAAD are on the curated PDAC list of TCGA 2017?
Who is the lead contact (corresponding author) of the TCGA 2017 PDAC paper in Cancer Cell?
What did Peran et al. 2018 show about TCGA-PAAD, and why does cross-validation not fix it?
cards.answer_md: TCGA-PAAD contains 33 profiles that are normal / pseudo-normal pancreas or not ductal adenocarcinoma, incl. eight neuroendocrine tumours whose patients live much longer. Genes separating them look prognostic. Cross-validation resamples the same contaminated cohort, so the spurious association survives; only removing them (the 150-sample list) helps.

cards.question_md: Which tumour type hidden in TCGA-PAAD creates spurious survival genes, according to Peran 2018?
Which method and material did Puleo et al. 2018 use to define five PDAC subtypes?

options.text_md: Independent component analysis on 309 FFPE resection specimens (Affymetrix HG-U219, E-MTAB-6134)
NMF on fresh-frozen RNA-seq of TCGA-PAAD

cards.question_md: Name the five Puleo subtypes from best to worst survival.
cards.answer_md: Pure classical (43.1 months), immune classical (37.4), desmoplastic (24.3), stroma activated (20.2), pure basal-like (10.3) - five regions on the tumour × stroma plane.

cards.question_md: Which ArrayExpress accession holds the Puleo 2018 FFPE cohort, the largest open PDAC cohort with survival?
What did Maurer et al. 2019 do experimentally that Moffitt 2015 did computationally, and what was the result?
cards.answer_md: They physically separated tumour epithelium and stroma by laser capture microdissection (60 matched pairs, 110 stroma profiles, GSE93326) and found the same classical / basal-like epithelial axis, the strongest evidence that the axis is not an NMF artefact. The stroma axis became ECM-rich vs immune-rich.

cards.question_md: Which lab published ADVOCATE?

options.text_md: Olive and Califano labs, Columbia University (Maurer et al. 2019, Gut)
Moffitt lab, Stony Brook (Torre-Healy et al. 2023)
Verhaak lab, MD Anderson (Yoshihara et al. 2013)

cards.question_md: What does Maurer 2019 Figure 2D show about basal-like tumours in TCGA?
cards.answer_md: In bulk TCGA profiles basal-like tumours had a clearly higher epithelial fraction than classical ones (p ≈ 4e-6); in the ADVOCATE virtual epithelium the difference vanished (p = 0.32). Bulk subtype calls are thus partly purity calls - a good slide for the purity problem.

cards.question_md: Which paper showed that the classical and basal-like programmes coexist within the same tumour, defining basal-like A/B, hybrid and classical A/B?
Which genomic events push a PDAC towards the basal-like end according to Chan-Seng-Yue 2020?
cards.answer_md: Allelic imbalance / amplification of mutant KRAS (higher mutant KRAS dosage); GATA6 amplification is instead enriched in classical tumours, so low GATA6 marks basal-like. Basal-like A is rare in resectable disease but about a quarter of stage IV.

cards.question_md: What does a PurIST probability of about 0.5 mean in the light of Chan-Seng-Yue 2020?
cards.answer_md: Not necessarily uncertainty about one true class: subtypes are a continuum and both programmes can coexist in one tumour (the hybrid region), so a mid probability can describe a genuinely mixed tumour.

cards.question_md: Which institute and consortium does the Chan-Seng-Yue 2020 cohort (ICGC PACA-CA, COMPASS biopsies) come from?

options.text_md: Ontario Institute for Cancer Research / PanCuRx, Toronto (Notta, Gallinger)

cards.question_md: What did Torre-Healy et al. 2023 conclude after applying all published PDAC schemes to all curated cohorts in pdacR?
cards.answer_md: Only the two-subtype (classical / basal-like) signatures and PurIST stay tumour-cell specific across purities and sample types. ADEX and exocrine-like track low tumour cellularity and mark acinar cell carcinomas; the immunogenic set overlaps the progenitor set. Hence "supports a two-subtype model".

cards.question_md: In Torre-Healy 2023 Figure 2a, how does the Bailey ADEX gene-set score relate to ABSOLUTE purity in TCGA-PAAD?

options.text_md: Negatively (Spearman ρ ≈ -0.26): low purity predicts high ADEX

cards.question_md: Which published PDAC model compares eight gene pairs within one sample?
What does the acronym PurIST stand for?
Who published PurIST, and in which journal?

options.text_md: Rashid et al. 2020 (Yeh lab, UNC), Clinical Cancer Research

cards.question_md: How does PurIST compute its output for one sample?
cards.answer_md: For each of eight gene pairs (one basal-like gene, one classical gene) it records whether the first gene is expressed higher than the second (a 0/1 indicator); a logistic regression over the eight indicators gives the probability of basal-like. The published threshold is 0.5.

cards.question_md: Why is PurIST robust to normalisation, platform and (largely) tumour purity?
cards.answer_md: It only asks which gene of a pair is higher within the same profile; library size, platform scale and global shifts change both genes alike and leave the order unchanged. Purity cancels as long as both genes of a pair come from the tumour compartment.

cards.question_md: Which cohorts trained PurIST?

options.text_md: GSE71729 (Moffitt), TCGA-PAAD and the Aguirre biopsies

cards.question_md: Name at least four of PurIST's eight gene pairs.
cards.answer_md: GPR87-REG4, KRT6A-ANXA10, BCAR3-GATA6, PTGES-CLDN18, ITGA3-LGALS4, C16orf74-DDC, S100A2-SLC40A1, KRT5-CLRN3 (basal-like gene first, classical gene second).

cards.question_md: What are the licence and code conditions of PurIST?
cards.answer_md: The fitted classifier object and `apply_classifier()` are on GitHub (naimurashid/PurIST), no training code. PurIST is patented and licensed to GeneCentric Technologies; use is free for not-for-profit research only. The authors require TPM or FPKM input for RNA-seq.

cards.question_md: What does PurIST's reported AUC of 0.993 measure - and what does it not measure?
cards.answer_md: Agreement with consensus-clustering subtype calls across six validation cohorts (meta-analysis) - i.e. reproducing the label of the scheme it was built from, not predicting an outcome. Survival evidence is separate (basal-like HR 1.90 for OS in pooled non-training samples).

cards.question_md: Which published PDAC model is a continuous score from basal-like (negative) to classical (positive)? (acronym)
On which material was the PAMG gradient derived?
What are the main limitations of PAMG for a clinical trial?
cards.answer_md: It is continuous with no published threshold, so a trial must fix one (fixing it on trial data is the classic error); hazard ratios are per ICA unit and not comparable with per-SD values; no discrimination metric (C-index) and no prospective validation are published.

cards.question_md: Which research group stands behind both the Puleo subtypes and PAMG?

options.text_md: The Marseille / Paris group around Rémy Nicolle and the CIT programme (Ligue contre le cancer)
The UNC group of Jen Jen Yeh
The Columbia group of Ken Olive

cards.question_md: Which two published PDAC models can be applied to a single new sample, and why not the others?
cards.answer_md: PurIST (within-sample gene pairs) and PAMG (projection against a fixed reference). The others need the whole cohort (clustering, centroids after scaling), need other material (microdissection, high purity) or exist only as gene lists without a rule.

cards.question_md: Where is pdacR hosted?

options.text_md: GitHub rmoffitt/pdacR (archived on Zenodo), web app now at Emory

cards.question_md: How do you restrict TCGA-PAAD to the 150 true PDAC in the pdacR app?
cards.answer_md: Filter samples by "Decision" and keep only "whitelist" (TCGA-PAAD has 182 samples there, 150 of them PDAC).

cards.question_md: Describe the recipe shared by the six PDAC immune-signature papers.
cards.answer_md: Immune genes from ImmPort / MSigDB (often filtered tumour vs normal against GTEx) → univariate Cox per gene on OS in TCGA-PAAD at an uncorrected p < 0.001-0.05 → LASSO-Cox → risk score → split at the median or an optimised cut-point in the same data → KM, log-rank, time-dependent ROC → external cohort re-standardised and often re-split.

cards.question_md: Name the recurring faults of the immune-signature recipe.
cards.answer_md: Genes are screened with the survival times of the very patients evaluated (of 1500 genes ~75 pass p < 0.05 by chance); in-sample cut-points; hazard ratios and log-rank p reported as performance; no comparison with all genes, the clinical variables or the subtype axis; validation models not frozen; tumour purity never adjusted for, so the score may measure the leukocyte fraction.

cards.question_md: Which of the six PDAC immune-signature papers had no external validation cohort at all?
Which immune-signature paper is the only one claiming to identify patients who benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy?
Why is Qian 2021's claim of adjuvant-chemotherapy benefit only a hypothesis?
cards.answer_md: A treatment-benefit claim is predictive and needs comparable treated and untreated patients; in retrospective cohorts the fitter patients receive chemotherapy, so the comparison is confounded by the indication. The checkpoint / PD-1 inference rests on no treated patients at all.

cards.question_md: Which gene appears in the immune scores of Yan 2020, Liu 2021, Li 2022 and Zhou 2022?
Why are the recurring genes (IL20RB, MET, ERAP2) across the immune signatures not independent confirmation?
cards.answer_md: All papers select from overlapping gene pools on the same TCGA-PAAD patients, so they find the same chance-and-composition winners; a later score beating an earlier one in TCGA-PAAD has beaten it on data both were fitted on.

cards.question_md: Which two immune-signature papers relate their score to tumour purity at all, and what did they find?
cards.answer_md: Zhou 2022 correlated IRGPI with the ESTIMATE purity value; Yan 2020 found purity higher in its high-risk group - what the purity objection predicts. Neither adjusts for purity; the other four do not measure it.

cards.question_md: What does IRGPI stand for?
Who published IRGPI, in which journal and year?

options.text_md: Zhou et al. 2022, Cancers (University of Debrecen)
Li et al. 2022, Precision Clinical Medicine
Wang et al. 2021, BMC Medical Genomics

cards.question_md: How many genes does IRGPI use?
Which twelve genes make up IRGPI? (name as many as you can)
cards.answer_md: FYN, MET, LRSAM1, PSPN, ERAP2, S100A1, IL20RB, MAP3K14, SEMA6C, PRKCG, CXCL11, GH1 - the largest weights are GH1 (-0.36), MET (+0.21) and PSPN (-0.20).

cards.question_md: Against which signatures did Zhou 2022 compare IRGPI?

options.text_md: A ferroptosis and a pyroptosis signature only

cards.question_md: Which immune-signature paper reported the highest (in-sample) time-dependent AUCs (0.85-0.93) of the genre, a warning sign of in-sample evaluation?
Which PDAC immune signature was the first of the six, and what was its gene list?
cards.answer_md: Yan et al. 2020 (Oncology Letters): four genes OAS1, MET, IL1R2, IL20RB, with a cut-point of 4.15 optimised in TCGA-PAAD and carried unchanged into ICGC PACA-AU and GSE62452.

cards.question_md: Which immune signature lists MET, ERAP2, IL20RB, EREG and SHC2 and validated in four cohorts?
Which paper is the single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 24 primary PDAC and 11 control pancreata with a malignant "ductal cell type 2"?
Under which Genome Sequence Archive accession are the Peng 2019 PDAC single-cell data deposited?
Which method estimates tumour purity from DNA copy-number and allele frequencies, and was used by TCGA 2017?
How does ESTIMATE turn an expression profile into a purity estimate, and what is its weakness?
cards.answer_md: Two gene signatures (stromal, immune) are scored by single-sample GSEA; their sum, the ESTIMATE score, is converted to purity by a formula calibrated against ABSOLUTE. Weakness: it is itself a gene-set score, so any stroma / immune gene set correlates with it through the mixture; it estimates composition, not expression per cell.

cards.question_md: Who published ESTIMATE?

options.text_md: Yoshihara et al. 2013, Nature Communications (Verhaak lab, MD Anderson)
Aran et al. 2015, Nature Communications (Butte lab)

cards.question_md: What did Aran, Sirota & Butte 2015 show about tumour purity?
cards.answer_md: Across ~10,000 TCGA samples of 21 cancer types, purity estimates from ESTIMATE, ABSOLUTE, LUMP and pathology were combined into a consensus purity estimate (CPE); purity correlated with many genes and confounded differential expression and survival associations, and pathologists' estimates ran higher than genomic ones.

cards.question_md: Which classifier principle, introduced by Geman et al. 2004 and extended by Tan et al. 2005, underlies PurIST?

options.text_md: (k-)top-scoring pairs: which gene of a pair is higher within one sample

cards.question_md: What does MCP-counter (Becht et al. 2016) estimate?

options.text_md: Abundance scores of eight immune and two stromal cell populations, comparable across samples
Absolute tumour purity from copy number
Cell-type proportions that sum to one within each sample
